children: shares slipped about 2% in premarket trading on Friday after Bank of America downgraded the sportswear maker to Underperform from Neutral, saying the company’s turnaround is taking longer to materialize as weakness in its larger lifestyle categories overshadows product innovation.
Analyst Lorraine Hutchinson cut its price target to $30 from $47, representing about 17% downside from the stock's last close.

They also lowered its fiscal 2027 and 2028 EPS estimates by 11% and 12%, respectively, to $1.43 and $1.87. It now expects “negative sales growth through F27,” pushing the sales turnaround into fiscal 2028.

The brokerage said North American wholesale growth has not been matched by sell-through, with declines in classic styles and some new launches putting “forward order books at risk” as retailers become more cautious.
Greater China sales fell 17% in the latest quarter, while its planned reduction in e-commerce partner distribution could add near-term pressure.
BofA said earnings increasingly depend on gross-margin expansion and cost control, while dividend coverage is stretched, with its fiscal 2027 forecast implying a 107% payout ratio.
The brokerage said further multiple compression was possible given limited visibility into a durable recovery.

title: BofA downgrades Nike to Underperform, cuts PT to $30
